REVIVAL MEETS ARCHITECTURE AS CHRISTIANITY RISES IN THE GLOBAL SOUTH

Pentecostalism and Megachurch Growth in Nigeria and the Philippines: A Comparative Chronicle

Daniel Breakforth

In the unfolding story of global Christianity, Nigeria and the Philippines stand out as two nations where Pentecostal revivalism has deeply reshaped not only the religious landscape but also the architectural and cultural fabric of society. Though far apart in geography, they share striking similarities in the way indigenous movements, spiritual fervor and visionary leadership have birthed megachurches that now command global attention.

The Nigerian Awakening

The Pentecostal wave in Nigeria began in earnest in the early 20th century, first influenced by foreign missionary groups, then maturing into an indigenous force. Movements such as The Apostolic Church (Iran Ologo) and Christ Apostolic Church laid early foundations, blending African spiritual vitality with Pentecostal doctrine. The revival intensified in the 1970s and 1980s as charismatic leaders emerged with bold visions and mass evangelism campaigns.

Among them were Archbishop Benson Andrew Idahosa, Pastor Enoch Adeboye of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor W.F. Kumuyi of Deeper Life Bible Church, Bishop David Oyedepo of Living Faith Church (Winners’ Chapel), Pastor Chris Oyakhilome of Christ Embassy and Dr. Daniel Olukoya of Mountain of Fire and Miracles Ministries. These leaders overtime fostered large-scale gatherings, crusades and teachings that captivated millions. The movement’s emphasis on healing, prosperity, spiritual warfare and personal encounter with the Holy Spirit resonated with Nigerians seeking hope amid political and economic uncertainties.

The Filipino Fire

In the Philippines, the Pentecostal revival was ignited through early 20th-century American missionary work. Over time, it evolved into a robust indigenous movement. From the 1970s onward, figures such as Brother Mike Velarde of El Shaddai, Brother Eddie Villanueva of Jesus Is Lord Church Worldwide and Pastor Apollo Quiboloy of Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KJV) rose to prominence, leading dynamic faith communities that emphasized healing, prophecy, and miraculous intervention.

These churches became more than religious spaces — they grew into political, cultural and social hubs. While Catholicism remained dominant, the vibrant worship styles, television outreach and energetic prayer rallies of the Pentecostal groups drew increasing numbers, especially among the urban poor and working class. The Filipino Pentecostal ethos is often marked by a fusion of charismatic worship and deep devotion, infused with nationalistic zeal. Interestingly, one of the most talked about Cardinals during the recent Conclave, Cardinal Tagle, is a Filipino. 

Architectural Testimonies of Faith

The Pentecostal revival in both countries birthed not just spiritual renewal but awe-inspiring physical structures. Nigeria became known for constructing some of the largest church auditoria in the world. Living Faith Church’s Faith Tabernacle was completed in 1999 and held the world record for the largest church auditorium at the time. It was later surpassed by the Glory Dome in Abuja, built by Dunamis International Gospel Centre, which became the first fully enclosed church building to seat over 100,000 worshippers. It was dedicated in 2018.

Meanwhile, Salvation Ministries’ Hand of God Cathedral in Port Harcourt nears completion and is already being hailed for its ambitious scale and architectural sophistication. Even grander is “The Ark,” a massive project by Living Faith Church, set to become a hub for global Christian gatherings. None of these however compares in magnitude to the scale of the RCCG's 'Open Canopy'-the 3km by 3km Arena which is better seen than told.

data.text:
Ferry Building, San Francisco
California, 1926 vs. 2025

One of the historic landmarks in all of San Francisco, the Ferry Building opened in 1898 (also, the same year Spain ceded the Philippines to the US for a sum of $20 million under the Treaty of Paris), and has since existed to this day for 127 years. 

Note that in the LEFT PHOTO below (circa 1926), the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge traversing the Yerba Buena Island is not yet visible. It would be completed and opened to traffic ten years after, or in 1936.

The Ferry Building is currently one of the popular culinary and events destinations. 

TIP: In Ferry Building, visit the Hog Island Oyster Co., which I highly recommend for its fine selection of oysters, variety of fresh seafood, the Hog Island Clam Chowder, and craft cocktails, as you dine by the beautiful waterfront setting.

#CaliforniaTravel

Nagsagawa ang Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) ng isang public consultation sa motorcycle community kaugnay sa implementasyon ng No Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP), motorcycle lane, bicycle lane, iba pang batas trapiko. 

Dinaluhan ng mga liders ng motorcycle groups, motorcycle taxi operators, transportation network vehicle services,  at motorcycle ride-hailing app firms ang public consultation na inorganisa kasama ng Department of Transportation, Land Transportation Office at Angkas. 

Nagbigay-daan ito para sagutin ni MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes, kasama sina MMDA General Manager Procopio Lipana at Traffic Discipline Office (TDO) Director for Enforcement Atty. Victor Nuñez ang mga inihayag na saloobin, kahilingan, at suhestiyon ng mga rider groups. 

"Mag-usap tayo nang maayos dahil hindi n'yo kami kaaway bagkus ay katulong n'yo kami... Ang gusto natin ay kaligtasan, disiplina, at mapabilis ang daloy ng trapiko para sa lahat," saad ni Artes sa mga rider groups. 

Nagpasalamat si Chairman Atty. Artes sa pagsuporta nila sa NCAP at sinabing bukas ang ahensiya sa mga suhestiyon sa pamamagitan ng kanilang mga lider. 

Iprinisinta rin ng MMDA ang pinag-aaralan na interventions sa Commonwealth Avenue sa Quezon City para sa kapakinabangan ng lahat ng dumadaan dito. Ayon kay Artes, ilalatag nila ang kanilang plano sa DOTr, Quezon City city government, at mga grupo ng siklista.  

Sinabi naman ni GM Lipana na hindi nagtatapos ang diyalogo ang kanilang pag-uusap dahil tuloy-tuloy ang kanilang pagtutulungan para sa kaayusan ng lansangan sa Metro Manila. 

Saad naman ni Angkas co-founder at CEO George Royeca, mahalaga ang pagkakaroon ng bukas na komunikasyon sa pagitan ng MMDA at mga rider groups.

To achieve an advocacy-oriented student council that puts pro-people governance at its core, the social context warrants an unrelenting act of challenging social systems, one that would fight back against oppressors, one that would rally along with the underserved.   

With the persisting scarcity of student representation that happens against the backdrop of political chaos and worsening state of healthcare, the challenge is clear: field and elect student leaders who would carry local and national campaigns from UP Manila and beyond.   

This year, The Manila Collegian presents #BotoUPM2025, the publication’s official coverage of the UP Manila General Student Elections, which will bring you updates straight from your local colleges and the scrutiny of the candidates vying for the highest decision-making student body in the university.
